cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Chaos ≠ order – complete disorder and confusion; a total lack of organization.

p.em: Example: When we try to celebrate Pandemonium Day without plans, delightful chaos fills our home.

cosy-blockquote.p: Predictable ≠ Surprising – easy to guess or know before it happens ≠ unexpected and causing wonder.

p.em: Example: A predictable office routine keeps us organized, but a surprising adventure keeps us alive.

cosy-blockquote.p: Spontaneous – done naturally without planning or preparation.

p.em: Example: We made a spontaneous decision to swap roles and completely ignore our strict schedule.

cosy-blockquote.p: Energetic – full of energy, life, and enthusiasm.

p.em: Example: The energetic crowd at the street festival chanted songs and celebrated spontaneous joy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Routine – a regular, everyday way of doing things.

p.em: Example: Breaking your morning routine on Pandemonium Day is the best way to invite creativity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Confusion – a state of not understanding something clearly or being mixed up.

p.em: Example: In the middle of the initial confusion, we discovered that playing without rules is highly educational.

cosy-blockquote.p: Thrilling – very exciting, positive, and pleasing.

p.em: Example: Embracing the happy accident of a missed flight can lead to a thrilling and unforgettable journey.

cosy-blockquote.p: Organization – the systematic structure, arrangement, or planning of an activity.

p.em: Example: While some activities require strict organization, Pandemonium Day thrives on the complete absence of it.
Example: Her desk is wonderfully messy, covered with notes and mugs that inspire her next big design.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unexpected – not expected or foreseen; surprising and unplanned.

p.em: Example: The unexpected success of our chaotic party proved that we do not always need a perfect plan.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
If you woke up tomorrow and found your city in complete chaos because all rules had disappeared, what would you do first?
★ Do you find a little chaos in your daily life fun or stressful? When does it become too much?

If your daily life became 100% predictable and every single hour was planned, how long would you survive before going crazy?
★ What is the most surprising thing that has happened to you recently?

If you could make one completely spontaneous decision right now without worrying about money or time, what would it be?
★ Are you usually a spontaneous traveler or a detailed planner?

If you designed the world's most energetic festival to celebrate Pandemonium Day, what wild activities would you include?
★ How do you feel when you are in a very loud, energetic crowd?

If a friend asked you to break your morning routine for one day to do something completely crazy, would you agree?
★ What is the most boring part of your daily routine?

If you received a mysterious letter in a language you don't speak, would you feel absolute confusion or excitement?
★ How do you usually handle moments of confusion in your workplace?

If you woke up to find everyone in your office had swapped jobs without warning, would you find it thrilling or terrifying?
★ What is the most thrilling adventure you have ever had?

If we removed all strict organization from public transport for a day, how would people get to work?
★ Is your desk currently a model of perfect organization, or is it a bit of a mess?

If you had to choose between living in a perfectly clean but boring room and a messy room full of art, which would you pick?
★ Does a messy kitchen make you angry or relaxed?

If an unexpected guest knocked on your door at midnight to celebrate Pandemonium Day, how would you welcome them?
★ Do you enjoy unexpected changes to your weekend plans?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If every office celebrated Pandemonium Day once a year, employees would embrace healthy chaos and become much more creative.
★ If you could declare one day of absolute chaos at your work, what rule would you eliminate first?

If modern cities became completely predictable and sterile, citizens would intentionally break harmless rules to feel alive.
★ If you woke up tomorrow and realized your day was 100% predictable, how would you feel?

If schools replaced strict grades with spontaneous play, children would grow up to be much more confident and happy.
★ If you could make a spontaneous career change today, what profession would you choose?

If communities built giant, chaotic playgrounds for adults, neighborhoods would feel much more energetic and united.
★ If you were invited to a wild, energetic street parade, would you join in?

If families spent one day a week without making any plans, breaking every routine, they would enjoy each other's company more.
★ If you could break one daily routine permanently, which one would it be?

If a sudden computer glitch changed everyone's job titles for a day, the initial confusion would lead to hilarious memories.
★ If your boss got your name and title wrong in a major meeting, how would you clear up the confusion?

If restaurants let customers invent the menu on the spot, dining out would become a thrilling, unpredictable experience.
★ If you could have one thrilling, unplanned dish right now, what would you want to eat?

If society completely abandoned strict organization for a week, we would discover that humans are naturally cooperative.
★ If you had to run a massive event without any pre-planned organization, how would you start?

If everyone intentionally kept a messy, unstructured desk, productivity would actually increase due to high creative flow.
★ If someone complained that your workspace was too messy, how would you defend yourself?

If we embraced unexpected changes of plans as blessings, daily stress levels in modern cities would drop to zero.
★ If you could design an unexpected surprise party for a close friend, what theme would you choose?

ul.li: Incorrect: We had a very chaos meeting yesterday. → Correct: We had a very chaotic meeting yesterday. ((Word class: 'chaos' is a noun; use the adjective 'chaotic' to describe the meeting.))

Incorrect: I am not comfortable to work in disorder. → Correct: I am not comfortable working in disorder. ((Gerund construction: the adjective phrase 'comfortable' is followed by a gerund 'working'.))

Incorrect: Our plans were cancelling because of the storm. → Correct: Our plans were canceled because of the storm. ((Passive voice: use the past participle 'canceled' instead of the present participle 'cancelling' for completed actions.))
